findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot remains a white canvas, and the platform probe reports computed colorScheme "normal" with no matching modern theming CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare light/dark support on the root and apply preference-driven surface tokens with color-scheme and prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Carousel and route state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found no view-transition CSS while the home screenshot shows a stateful carousel and the site exposes navigable ranking/article states.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for carousel/state changes and cross-document transitions for compatible navigations, with reduced-motion fallbacks.

findings.summary: Long pages provide no scroll-state-aware orientation.
findings.evidence: The home document is 12,706 CSS px tall, but the CSS probe found no scroll-state/container-query features and the captured chrome is static.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a restrained scroll progress or scroll-state-aware header treatment on long content and article pages.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures article content and even the 404 recovery page on load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile article screenshots show a centered consent wall dimming the entire article; the same wall covers the tested 404 page.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-essential consent UI, keep core content readable, and use a compact, clearly dismissible consent surface with equivalent accept/decline choices.

findings.summary: Consent overlays are custom div dialogs without complete modal semantics.
findings.evidence: The article probe found four DIV elements with role=dialog, none with aria-modal; the page uses no native dialog or popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog for the modal consent flow, ensure one active dialog, correct labelling, focus containment/restoration, and platform dismissal behavior.

findings.summary: Legacy article templates omit the viewport meta tag and render a desktop canvas on mobile.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360px viewport, the article reports no viewport meta, a 1120px layout viewport, scale 0.321, and client width 980; the screenshot is an unreadably scaled desktop page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width=device-width, initial-scale=1 and rebuild the article template with intrinsic, fluid layout and mobile reflow rather than shrink-to-fit.

findings.summary: Reusable surfaces rely on viewport behavior rather than component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules across the home surface, while cards and ranking components are reused in distinct widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Define containment on reusable card/list regions and use size container queries where component layout changes independently of the viewport.

findings.summary: The homepage has a very slow lab LCP.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 16.9s, FCP 4.7s, Speed Index 7.2s, and performance 0.59; the independent trace measured LCP 4.04s and FCP 1.77s, confirming load sensitivity despite low TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce document latency, and defer non-critical images and third-party work; validate on mobile throttling and field data.

findings.summary: Heavy images and blocking chains delay primary content.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 3.54MB across 73 requests, including 2.85MB of images; Lighthouse estimated 2,496KiB image savings, 1,600ms render-blocking savings, and 1,270ms document-latency savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Resize and encode images responsively, preload only the true LCP image, defer below-fold media, and shorten critical CSS/document latency.

findings.summary: Unused and third-party JavaScript adds avoidable load cost.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 209KiB unused JavaScript and 20KiB legacy JavaScript; HAR shows roughly 513KB from Google Tag Manager resources among a 629KB script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics loaders, conditionally load non-essential integrations, and ship modern, route-scoped bundles.

findings.summary: Some controls and graphics have incorrect or missing accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility 0.96 failed visible-label/name matching and found an SVG with role=img but no accessible alternative; the image audit also flagged 52 images without alt attributes, requiring decorative versus meaningful review.
findings.suggestedFix: Align accessible names with visible labels, hide decorative SVGs from the accessibility tree, and provide useful alternatives for meaningful images.

findings.summary: Heading and list semantics are malformed on the homepage.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found an empty H1, while Lighthouse found LI elements whose parent role is not list and reported a malformed accessibility tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the page a meaningful H1, preserve native list semantics in the carousel, and re-test heading/landmark order with axe and keyboard navigation.

findings.summary: Article pages fail mobile reflow and present text at an unreadable scale.
findings.evidence: The 360px article capture uses a 1120px layout viewport at 0.321 scale because the template has no viewport meta tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore standards-based viewport configuration and ensure article, profile, consent, and sidebar content reflows at 320 CSS px and at 200% zoom.

findings.summary: Images lack intrinsic dimensions and many are oversized or legacy encoded.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found all 100 images without width/height attributes, 25 oversized, 58 without srcset, and 75 in legacy formats; Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width and height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, and modern encodings while preserving correct alternatives.

findings.summary: Third-party code uses a deprecated API and the page blocks BFCache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports deprecated Attribution Reporting usage from a Google tag and three BFCache failure reasons, including Cache-Control: no-store after cookie mutation.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or remove the deprecated tag behavior and review cache/cookie policies so eligible navigations can use BFCache.

findings.summary: Representative article pages omit a meta description.
findings.evidence: The article probe reports description=null although the title and canonical are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate a unique description from the article summary or opening content and keep it consistent with visible copy.

findings.summary: The conventional root sitemap URL returns 404.
findings.evidence: The robots/sitemap probe received HTTP 404 for https://ameblo.jp/sitemap.xml; robots.txt was available and representative pages had canonicals.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish or advertise the appropriate sitemap index in robots.txt, including public article and listing templates.

findings.summary: The public portal homepage has social tags but no entity structured data.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found seven Open Graph tags but zero JSON-LD blocks on the homepage; the article correctly exposes BlogPosting JSON-LD.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite structured data to the portal while preserving article-specific BlogPosting markup.

findings.summary: Transport is HTTPS, but security headers and cookie attributes are weak.
findings.evidence: Headers show CSP only as upgrade-insecure-requests with no HSTS; three analytics cookies are not Secure and all four captured cookies use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy an enforcing nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, and Secure/SameSite attributes appropriate to each cookie; verify auth cookies separately as HttpOnly.

findings.summary: The public homepage loads a broad tracking footprint before a consent choice is shown there.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence found 15 third-party origins and Google Analytics, DoubleClick, Google Ads, and GTM; HAR attributes 72 of 73 requests and 3.51MB to non-main origins under the tool’s registrable-origin classification.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential tracking on consent, consolidate analytics, minimize event collection, and audit each third party for necessity and retention.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defense policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The header probe found no HSTS, no X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors, no Referrer-Policy, and a Permissions-Policy that only delegates ch-ua-full.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, frame-ancestors, strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy; expand CSP beyond upgrade-insecure-requests.

findings.summary: Article content is crowded by legacy chrome and consent UI.
findings.evidence: The desktop article capture devotes substantial space to policy chrome, breadcrumbs, search/profile sidebars, and a full modal before the article can be read; mobile simply scales all of it down.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a content-first article template with responsive progressive disclosure for secondary chrome and a non-obscuring consent treatment.

findings.summary: Image delivery is disproportionate for a portal homepage.
findings.evidence: Images account for 2.85MB of the 3.54MB transfer; 25 are oversized, 75 use legacy formats, and Lighthouse estimates 2,496KiB savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate correctly sized AVIF/WebP variants, use srcset/sizes, and avoid loading below-fold promotional media at desktop resolutions.

findings.summary: Analytics and advertising perform avoidable background requests.
findings.evidence: The HAR records multiple analytics, in-view measurement, conversion, and cookie-sync requests, including redirect chains across Ameba and Google origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Batch essential analytics, defer background fetches, remove redundant tags, and stop cookie-sync/conversion work until consent and user value justify it.

findings.summary: Third-party and promotional media dominate the network budget.
findings.evidence: HAR attributes 3.51MB to origins other than the main origin, led by 2.09MB from static-lifestyle.ameba.jp and about 513KB from Google Tag Manager; several images individually exceed 600KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template third-party and image budgets, self-host or remove unnecessary dependencies, and lazy-load promotional media near the viewport.

taskList.title: Replace the legacy article viewport/layout with a responsive, reflowing template
Remove the blocking consent wall and rebuild it with complete native dialog semantics
Cut LCP and transfer weight through responsive image delivery and critical-path work
Gate and consolidate tracking, then minimize third-party/background work
Deploy complete security headers and hardened cookie attributes
Repair names, SVG alternatives, H1, list semantics, and image dimensions
Complete metadata and sitemap coverage across portal and article templates
Add preference-aware dark theming and restrained navigation transitions
Remove deprecated tag usage and restore BFCache eligibility
